headline: Bookings surge and margins expand; sales outlook trimmed
summary_short: Flowserve's Q2 2026 diluted EPS rose 24.2% y/y to $0.77 (adjusted $0.95) as bookings jumped 26% y/y to $1.35B, even as reported sales dipped 1.6% y/y to $1,169.2M; management cut full-year organic sales guidance to about -1% on Middle East disruption while raising the low end of adjusted EPS guidance to $4.05-$4.20.
summary_long: Operating margin expanded 70bp to 13.0% (adjusted 15.3%), helped by a $27.7M non-cash gain on the FAMCO equity remeasurement, even as reported sales dipped 1.6% y/y to $1,169.2M (organic -3.3%). Flow Control Division gross margin fell to 24.8% (from 29.0%) on $22.5M of realignment charges tied to the Trillium/FAMCO integrations. Cash from operations fell to $129.2M from $154.1M. Cash was $731.0M against long-term debt of $2,122.4M, up from $1,662.0M q/q after $499.3M of acquisition-related debt issuance; goodwill rose to $1,744.9M. Management cut full-year organic sales guidance to approximately -1% (from -1% to +2%) on Middle East disruption, while raising the low end of adjusted EPS guidance to $4.05-$4.20 (from $4.00-$4.20).

drivers.explanation: Grew in step with the 21% y/y rise in net earnings, plus a lower diluted share count (128.4M vs 131.6M y/y) after continued buybacks.
Consolidated gross margin fell to 32.9% (from 34.2% y/y) as Flow Control Division margin dropped to 24.8% (from 29.0%) on $22.5M of realignment charges; Pumps Division margin was roughly flat.
Boosted mainly by a $27.7M non-cash gain from remeasuring Flowserve's previously held equity interest in FAMCO upon closing that acquisition, booked in net earnings from affiliates.
Followed operating income higher and a smaller other-expense drag ($12.1M vs $25.0M y/y), partly offset by higher interest expense ($25.7M vs $20.3M y/y) from acquisition-related borrowing.
Q/q dip reflects capex, dividends and buybacks outrunning $129.2M of operating cash flow; the $517.7M FAMCO/Trillium purchase price was funded mostly by new debt, not cash.
Company-disclosed financing activity: $499.3M of senior notes issued plus net revolver draws year-to-date to fund the FAMCO and Trillium Valves acquisitions.
Retained earnings grew with net income, partly offset by a wider accumulated other comprehensive loss (-$607.3M vs -$575.4M) from foreign-currency translation.

CEO cited 26% bookings growth, record $696M aftermarket bookings, and margin expansion as proof of the Flowserve Business System and 3D growth strategy, with resilient demand in power, nuclear and energy security.
